title: Recording as a portfolio
summary: Record three takes of a piece, choose the best one, and say in a sentence why it beat the others.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: Three boxes stacked, one for each of the three recorded takes, listened to and compared side by side before choosing the best one and saying why it won.

steps.title: Recording as a portfolio
steps.body:
One recording tells you how one attempt went. Three recordings, listened to side by side, tell you something more useful. You can see what you are actually improving, sitting to sitting, and what a fair judge of your own playing sounds like.

1. Record take one straight through, whatever happens, no stopping and no do-over.
2. Listen back, pick the one thing take one showed most clearly, fix it, and record take two.
3. Listen back again, pick the next thing to fix, and record take three.
4. Listen to all three takes in a row and choose the best one, writing one sentence explaining why it won.

Choosing your own best take, and being able to say why, is a skill on its own. It is the same judgment a teacher uses, aimed at yourself.

figure.alt: The same three boxes, one take recorded and fixed at a time, each sitting listening back before recording the next.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: record take one, straight through, no stopping
Sitting 2: listen, fix one thing, record take two
Sitting 3: listen, fix the next thing, record take three
Sitting 4: listen to all three, choose the best, write why in the log
An old piece recorded once, just to add to the collection

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Play the piece once through for a fourth, final take, the version you send in, hands in the frame.
